Synthesis with SLOOS lens:
- Policy stance: The March 17, 2021 FOMC kept rates at 0–1/4 percent and continued asset purchases ($80B Treasuries, $40B agency MBS), reinforcing average-inflation targeting and an accommodative stance until maximum employment and inflation moderately above 2% are achieved.
- SLOOS cross-check: Bank lending conditions are mixed. Domestic banks reported soft C&I loan demand, while foreign banks saw some strengthening. Large banks eased standards for several mortgage categories (GSE-eligible, QM jumbo, QM non-jumbo non-GSE), supporting household credit. However, banks cited multiple headwinds—economic outlook, industry-specific problems, reduced risk tolerance, liquidity, supervisory and legislative concerns—limiting business credit appetite.
- Read-through: Fed policy and improving activity data support a cautiously positive tone, but the SLOOS shows a still-cautious business credit channel offset by easier mortgage credit. This tempers optimism relative to a purely policy-driven view.
